risks.title: Bounded builder visualization scanning or rendering causes a user-visible performance regression
risks.oracle: Same-environment Prism baseline/candidate measurements with identical scenario, Minecraft, Java, Fabric Loader and environment_id.
manual_evidence: Prism/JFR captures for all eight S-grade metrics in the same environment.
exit_criteria: All eight required performance metrics have at least three baseline and candidate samples.
Every metric remains within the S-grade regression budget.
Occluded Highlights scan budgets and loaded-chunk-only constraints remain enforced.

risks.title: Corrupt, hostile or migrated configuration prevents startup or contaminates another config domain
risks.oracle: Invalid input is rejected or sanitized to the documented safe default while unaffected configuration domains remain usable.
exit_criteria: Malformed, oversized, deeply nested and incompatible values fail safely.
Historical and future-schema fixtures preserve documented migration behavior.
A failure in one config domain does not reset unrelated domains.

risks.title: Placement Assist reports a BlockState that differs from vanilla placement semantics
risks.oracle: The actual BlockState produced by vanilla Minecraft placement is the oracle; production prediction formulas are not duplicated in the test.
exit_criteria: Supported placement families match or explicitly explain a vanilla adjustment.
Unsupported items and impossible placements do not invent a preview.
Dimension, timeout and session transitions clear stale comparison state.

risks.title: A runtime component or optional integration failure propagates into unrelated ChiseTweaks features
risks.oracle: Only the failing component is quarantined; healthy components continue and session cleanup remains possible.
manual_evidence: Prism smoke test with representative optional-mod combinations.
exit_criteria: RuntimeException and LinkageError are isolated at the component boundary.
Optional integrations remain fail-soft when their target mod is absent or incompatible.
Disconnect and dimension changes leave no stale session state.

risks.title: A release publishes a JAR that is not the exact artifact verified by CI
risks.oracle: Git tree SHA, runtime SHA-256, embedded metadata and release asset identity must agree with CI provenance.
exit_criteria: Release promotion uses the previously verified runtime JAR without rebuilding it.
Published SHA-256 matches the verified artifact.
The release tag points to the verified main commit.

risks.title: Automation, custom protocol ownership or background execution enters the client-only Tweaks product scope
risks.oracle: The executable product contract remains client-only and builder-oriented, with no custom play protocol or input automation.
exit_criteria: The compatibility registry remains exactly 16 low-level toggles while the product UI remains seven Tweaks groups.
No prohibited packet, input-injection or background-thread primitives are introduced.
Server installation remains unnecessary.

risks.title: Seven-group settings refactoring loses pending changes, misroutes persistence or makes a retained capability unreachable
risks.oracle: Settings behavior is defined by user-visible row bindings and persistence-domain results, not by private helper names.
manual_evidence: Prism GUI acceptance for narrow width, Japanese/English, scrolling and save failure feedback.
exit_criteria: Failed persistence domains remain pending while successful domains clear.
All retained capabilities remain reachable through the seven Tweaks product groups.
Screen code does not reacquire config-domain ownership.

risks.title: Handheld Size obscures gameplay, distorts non-first-person rendering or conflicts with the active resource pack
risks.oracle: When disabled or outside FIRST_PERSON_LEFT/RIGHT, rendering remains vanilla. When enabled, only the submitted first-person item pose is scaled while Minecraft retains model, texture, animation and input ownership.
manual_evidence: Prism acceptance with block items, generic items, tools/weapons, shield, main hand/offhand and a representative external resource pack.
exit_criteria: Disabled, GUI and non-first-person contexts retain scale factor 1.0.
Block, item and tool percentages remain bounded to 40-100%; shield remains near vanilla at 95%.
The feature ships no copied Small Handhelds model JSON or textures and does not replace the active resource pack.

risks.title: Legacy Lava/Hidden settings migration shrinks the user's previous occluded visualization coverage
risks.oracle: When legacy Lava and Hidden budgets differ, the shared Occluded Highlights migration preserves their union by taking larger ranges/result limits and the shorter interval before applying safety clamps.
exit_criteria: Legacy Lava-only and shared historical fixtures migrate successfully.
Differing legacy Lava/Hidden values preserve the documented union semantics.
Migrated values remain inside WorksiteVisibilityBudgetPolicy bounds.

risks.title: Villager Job Site visualization invents a workstation relation that Minecraft does not know
risks.oracle: A link is rendered only from MemoryModuleType.JOB_SITE in the current dimension; no workstation block scan or profession-based fallback inference exists.
manual_evidence: Prism acceptance with linked and currently unknown/unlinked villagers.
exit_criteria: Known JOB_SITE memory produces a link.
Missing JOB_SITE memory produces no guessed link.
No fallback workstation traversal is present in production.
